name: Project-75I
variant: Submarine procurement programme — 6 diesel-electric AIP attack submarines

header.one_liner: Indian Navy's programme to acquire six advanced diesel-electric attack submarines with Air-Independent Propulsion (AIP) and land-attack missiles; long-running procurement repeatedly deferred, partnering two Indian yards (MDL, L&T) with a foreign OEM.
header.maker: Programme — Indian Navy; two shortlisted Indian yards (MDL, L&T Shipbuilding) partnering a foreign diesel-electric submarine OEM
header.indigenous_label: AIP to be indigenised (DRDO fuel-cell) where feasible; design from a foreign OEM

what_it_is.prose: Project-75I is the Indian Navy's long-running programme to acquire six advanced diesel-electric attack submarines featuring Air-Independent Propulsion (AIP) and land-attack cruise missile capability, to be built in India. First mooted in the late 2000s and formally pursued as a strategic-partnership (SP) procurement, P-75I is a signature test of India's 'Make in India in the Strategic Partnership' model — under which two shortlisted Indian yards, Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited (MDL) and L&T (Larsen & Toubro) Shipbuilding, are to partner a foreign submarine OEM to build the six boats. The programme was repeatedly deferred through the 2010s and 2020s over cost, technology-transfer terms, the AIP requirement and the choice of partner/OEM. The boats are intended to be larger than the Scorpène/Kalvari class, with AIP for extended submerged endurance (a DRDO fuel-cell AIP is destined to be integrated) and a land-attack missile capability that the current P-75 boats lack. As of the mid-2020s, P-75I remained in procurement with a final OEM selection and yard partnership not yet finalised; it is the linchpin of India's ambition to rebuild its submarine force toward a ~18+ boat strength with genuinely modern, AIP-equipped boats. The programme is strategically important because it directly tests whether India can assemble cutting-edge submarines indigenously with meaningful technology transfer, versus the licenced Scorpène build it previously relied on.

deployments_procurement.summary: P-75I has gone through multiple procurement iterations since ~2007. Two Indian yards (MDL, L&T) were shortlisted to partner a foreign OEM. The programme has been deferred repeatedly over TOT, cost and AIP terms, and remains in procurement rather than contracted as of 2026 — significantly behind the Navy's original timeline. No boats have been laid down.

faq.question: What is Project-75I?
faq.answer: Project-75I is the Indian Navy's programme to acquire six advanced diesel-electric attack submarines with Air-Independent Propulsion (AIP) and land-attack missile capability, to be built in India at MDL or L&T under a strategic-partnership model with a foreign submarine OEM.

faq.question: Why has P-75I taken so long?
faq.answer: P-75I has been repeatedly deferred over the technology-transfer terms, cost, the AIP requirement and the choice of foreign OEM and Indian yard. As of 2026 it remains in procurement rather than contracted, significantly behind the Navy's original timeline.

faq.question: How does P-75I differ from the Kalvari class?
faq.answer: The Kalvari (P-75) class is a six-boat Scorpène design already in service. P-75I is a separate, newer programme for six larger submarines that add AIP (extended submerged endurance) and land-attack missile capability.
